documents.pageContent: And it came to pass that he had two sons. He gave unto the eldest the name of Nephi, and unto the youngest, the name of Lehi. And they began to grow up unto the Lord.

metadata.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 3:21** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records contention and dissensions in years 43–48, including migrations from Zarahemla to the land northward, settlement near large waters, cement building, shipping timber, and growth of cities and temples. It notes extensive Nephite recordkeeping and later Nephite decline. Helaman judges with justice, names sons Nephi and Lehi, and peace returns while Gadianton’s secret combinations persist. Many join the church by baptism; later pride brings persecution. Helaman dies; Nephi succeeds.

documents.pageContent: And my people would that we should call the name of the place Nephi; wherefore, we did call it Nephi.

metadata.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 5:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Nephi’s flight from angry brothers who seek his life, following the Lord’s warning. Nephi leads his family, Zoram, Sam, Jacob, Joseph, sisters, and believers into the wilderness, settles in a place called Nephi, and forms the people of Nephi who keep the law of Moses and prosper. Nephi makes weapons, teaches crafts, builds a temple, consecrates Jacob and Joseph as priests, describes Lamanites being cut off and cursed, and begins new plates amid later wars.

documents.pageContent: And all those who were with me did take upon them to call themselves the people of Nephi.

documents.pageContent: For I, Nephi, was constrained to speak unto them, according to his word; for I had spoken many things unto them, and also my father, before his death; many of which sayings are written upon mine other plates; for a more history part are written upon mine other plates.

metadata.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 4:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Lehi blessing the children of Laman and Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Sam, giving commandments about prosperity and being cut off. Lehi dies and is buried. Laman, Lemuel, and Ishmael’s sons become angry with Nephi. Nephi explains his writing purpose, recounts divine help, angels and visions, and offers prayers for deliverance, strength, and trust in God rather than man.

documents.pageContent: Wherefore, I, Nephi, to be obedient to the commandments of the Lord, went and made these plates upon which I have engraven these things.

documents.pageContent: And Nephi, who was the father of Nephi, who had the charge of the records, did not return to the land of Zarahemla, and could nowhere be found in all the land.

metadata.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 2:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records the people forgetting earlier signs, hardening their hearts, and growing in wickedness as years 95–100 pass, with time reckoned from the sign of Christ’s coming. Nephi, keeper of the records, does not return to Zarahemla and cannot be found. In the thirteenth year wars intensify with numerous Gadianton robbers; converted Lamanites unite with Nephites, are numbered as Nephites, and fight for safety and worship. Fighting continues through years 14–15 with shifting advantages and increasing afflictions.

documents.pageContent: And I, Nephi, had kept the records upon my plates, which I had made, of my people thus far.

documents.pageContent: I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents, therefore I was taught somewhat in all the learning of my father; and having seen many afflictions in the course of my days, nevertheless, having been highly favored of the Lord in all my days; yea, having had a great knowledge of the goodness and the mysteries of God, therefore I make a record of my proceedings in my days.

metadata.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 1:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Nephi’s introduction to his record and language, and sets the scene in the first year of Zedekiah at Jerusalem. Lehi prays, sees a pillar of fire, and receives a vision of heaven, a descending figure with twelve others, and a book. Reading it, he prophesies Jerusalem’s destruction and Babylonian captivity, and testifies of a coming Messiah. The people mock and seek Lehi’s life.

documents.pageContent: And now, I, Nephi, speak concerning the prophecies of which my father hath spoken, concerning Joseph, who was carried into Egypt.
